# McGill scope-ambiguity human evidence

Pinned source: https://github.com/McGill-NLP/scope-ambiguity at `3d00bad00c7b0c3775e69706f5322f44ff1ccff0`.

SUTRA vendors the final Experiment 1B, 2A and 2B base datasets byte-for-byte and stores a deterministic aggregate of the cleaned crowdsourced responses. Worker identifiers, comments, slide numbers and experiment-condition metadata are intentionally not retained. The upstream dataset README states that these final datasets underwent rounds of human validation; the human-results README describes the response files as cleaned crowdsourced results.

**Important exclusion:** upstream explicitly says Experiment 1A is subject to the copyright restrictions of the AnderBois et al. corpus and requires permission from the Law School Admission Council and Adrian Brasoveanu. SUTRA does not vendor Experiment 1A.

Upstream repository license: MIT, copyright 2024 McGill NLP. Paper: Gaurav Kamath, Sebastian Schuster, Sowmya Vajjala, Siva Reddy, “Scope Ambiguities in Large Language Models,” TACL 2024, DOI 10.1162/tacl_a_00670.

This is independent human evidence for scope-sensitive constructions, especially quantifier/indefinite, negation/quantifier, and quantificational-adverb interactions. It does not provide human labels for all 20 SUTRA ambiguity families and is not relabeled as such.
